longDescription:
Quest is where everything you are working on lives — software projects with a dozen repos, and everything else too.

• One model, three levels — projects hold epics, epics hold items, items hold subtasks. Every level below the epic is board-visible and independently tracked.
• Five surfaces — a cross-project Today inbox with quick capture, a project overview with links and activity, a filterable list, a drag-and-drop board, and a timeline with an unscheduled rail so nothing gets lost — an epic with its own dates keeps them, an epic without dates spans its scheduled children, and an epic with neither stays unscheduled.
• Per-project status schemes — each project carries its own set of statuses, which drive its board columns and its completion rollups. Completion follows a status's meaning rather than its name. Schemes start from the project's kind (software projects get an In Review column, general projects don't) and are editable per project afterwards: status ids are permanent, a scheme always needs a done status, and removing a status that still holds items reassigns them to a status you name.
• Built for the assistant — Quest publishes fifteen tools over MCP, so the agent files, moves, and queries real work items instead of writing markdown. Deletes are soft and every agent action is logged.
• Connected — link repos, branches, PRs, folders, and documents to any project or item. Multi-repo projects are the normal case.
